title: Promising Treatments and Novel Therapeutic Approaches for the Management of Necrotizing Enterocolitis.
abstract: Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is a deadly intestinal disease that most commonly occurs in premature infants. Current treatments are reactive rather than preventative, and include feeding cessation, antibiotics, gastric decompression, and supportive care. In severe NEC, surgical intervention is required for intestinal perforation or failure of medical management. Promising treatment modalities are being explored to prevent NEC and reduce NEC severity, including probiotics, probiotic delivery sy...

title: Efficacy of yeast mannan supplementation on increasing stool frequency in adults: a randomized controlled trial.
abstract: Yeast mannans are microbial-available substrates that may improve laxation and specifically modulate gut microbiota composition. The aim of this study is to determine the effect of yeast mannan supplementation on stool frequency in adults. Secondary aims will assess gastrointestinal tolerance and quality of life, whole gut transit time, fecal microbiota composition, and fecal and urinary levels of microbial-generated metabolites.

title: A randomized controlled double-blinded trial to assess the risk of gestational diabetes mellitus in non-anemic pregnant women who receive oral iron supplementation.
abstract: Pregnant women in India are routinely prescribed oral iron supplements as part of the national Anemia Mukt Bharat (AMB) program for anemia control. In women with iron-deficiency anemia, the benefits of iron supplementation during pregnancy, both for the mother and child, are very clear. In non-anemic pregnant women, however, the benefits of iron supplementation vis-à-vis associated risks that have been reported have not been studied adequately. Studies have suggested that iron may impair insulin...

title: Gastric microbiota‑derived postbiotics as antimicrobial and anti‑biofilm agents.
abstract: The human gastric microbiota is recognized as a diverse and metabolically active ecosystem with significant roles in health and disease. Beyond probiotics, postbiotics, non-viable microbial products with antimicrobial and anti-biofilm properties, offer stable and safer therapeutic alternatives. Rising antimicrobial resistance and biofilm associated infections caused by pathogens such as Staphylococcus aureus and Candida albicans highlight the urgent need for new strategies. Based on this evidenc...

title: An exploratory 12-week pilot study of gut microbiota and body-weight patterns during sodium nitrite exposure and Lactobacillus plantarum 299v supplementation in Wistar rats.
abstract: Sodium nitrite (E250) is a widely used additive in processed meat products and has been reported to disrupt the gut microbiota and exert carcinogenic effects via N-nitroso compounds. This exploratory pilot study examined body-weight and longitudinal gut-microbiota patterns during sodium nitrite exposure and Lactobacillus plantarum 299v supplementation in adolescent Wistar rats.

title: Glucosamine-Producing Engineered Probiotics Enhance the Immune Function of Microglia.
abstract: Dysregulated microglial activation underlies both neuroinflammation and neurodegenerative pathology. GlcN has well-documented anti-inflammatory activity across multiple cell types, yet whether it acts on microglia in any meaningful way has not been directly tested. Here we show that GlcN shifts microglia toward an M2 anti-inflammatory state by altering their metabolic program, an effect accompanied by a clear improvement in immune function. A practical barrier complicates direct translation of t...

title: Engineered Calprotectin-Responsive Probiotics for Inflammatory Bowel Disease Treatment.
abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a complex intestinal disorder for which effective treatment options remain limited. The modulation of gut microbiota balance using probiotics holds promise as a therapeutic approach to restore intestinal microenvironment homeostasis. However, the clinical translation of conventional probiotics is constrained by the suboptimal therapeutic efficacy. Here, we constructed a recombinant Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 strain (EcN-CR-IL2) based on an optimized calprote...

title: Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus-Derived Extracellular Vesicles Alleviate Colitis via PPAR Signaling and the Gut Microbiota-Metabolite Axis.
abstract: Intestinal barrier dysfunction is a hallmark of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), yet effective therapies remain limited, and the mechanisms of probiotic-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) are poorly understood. Using complementary cell, murine, and intestinal organoid models, we investigated the protective effects of Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus ZFML003-derived EVs (ZFML003-EVs). In Caco-2 cells, ZFML003-EVs restored barrier integrity by upregulating tight junction proteins (ZO-1, Occludin, C...
journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry

title: Tracking the Gastrointestinal Fate and Prebiotic Effect of Sparassis crispa Polysaccharide: In Vitro Dynamic Digestion Models.
abstract: Gastrointestinal digestion is indispensable for the utilization of bioactive macromolecules. Compared to static digestion models, dynamic digestion models more realistically simulate the physiological conditions of the gastrointestinal tract. In this study, the in vitro dynamic digestion system and fecal fermentation were used to systematically evaluate the digestive and fermentative properties ofSparassis crispa polysaccharide (SCP). During gastric digestion, the molecular weight of SCP decreas...
journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry

title: Biosynthesis of 3-Hydroxy-3-methylbutyrate by Probiotic Escherichia coli Nissle 1917.
abstract: 3-Hydroxy-3-methylbutyrate (HMB) is an important nutritional supplement for managing sarcopenia. This study engineered an HMB biosynthetic pathway in the probiotic Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 (EcN). The initial engineered strain exhibited low HMB titers, as carbon flux was primarily diverted toward acetate formation. Deleting the pyruvate oxidase gene (poxB) reduced acetate but caused significant pyruvate accumulation, revealing a severe kinetic bottleneck in endogenous pyruvate dehydrogenase (...
journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry

title: Probiotics-Driven Type I Photosensitizer for Tumor-Targeted Fluorescence Imaging and Photodynamic Immunotherapy.
abstract: The high morbidity and mortality of cancer have driven the medical community to continuously explore strategies for diagnosis and treatment. Photosensitizers (PSs) offer the possibility of simultaneous diagnosis and photodynamic therapy (PDT) for tumors with the advantages of noninvasiveness, high sensitivity, and minimum drug resistance. However, current PSs lack active tumor-targeting capability and systemic antitumor immune activity, leading to poor diagnostic and therapeutic efficacy, which ...

title: Mannose-cRGD Engineered Lactobacillus helveticus-Derived Exosomes Enhance Loaded Pterostilbene Bioavailability: From Dual Insights of Membrane Lipid Orderliness and Dual-Targeting Endocytosis Modulation.
abstract: Exosomes derived from probiotics are emerging as innovative oral nanocarriers but face challenges in targeted delivery and stability. Here, Lactobacillus helveticus-derived exosomes (LHexo) were dual-functionalized with mannose and cRGD (McRLHexo), yielding improved membrane lipid ordering, denser PEG brush layer, and distinct "cloud-like" surface nanostructure. McRLHexo exhibited enhanced stability under UV (transmittance reduction > 98%), thermal, and digestive conditions (drug retention >86%)...
journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry

title: Sugar Alcohol-Driven Synbiotic Confers Growth Promotion and Disease Resistance in Panax notoginseng.
abstract: The efficacy of synbiotic ("probiotic + prebiotic") strategies against soil-borne diseases is often limited by the low specificity of conventional prebiotics, which may also stimulate pathogens. Here, we developed a precision synbiotic system using a sugar alcohol mixture (SAs) as a selective substrate for the probiotic yeast Saitozyma podzolica (SP), while being poorly utilized by the root rot pathogen Ilyonectria vredehoekensis (I1). In Panax notoginseng, the synbiotic system simultaneously en...
journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry

title: Weissella confusa in fermented foods and beyond: A comprehensive review of probiotic functions, metabolite biosynthesis, stress adaptation, and application prospects.
abstract: Weissella confusa, a heterofermentative lactic acid bacterium widely distributed in fermented foods, plant surfaces, animal habitats, and the human gut, has emerged as a focal point of microbiological research becaues of its diverse metabolic functions, environmental resilience, and the potential probiotic traits exhibited by certain strains. This review summarizes current research on W. confusa from four dimensions: its probiotic-related functions and health-promoting mechanisms, key metabolite...

title: Egg-derived high internal phase emulsions enhance the viability and retention of probiotics during gastrointestinal digestion.
abstract: Although high internal phase emulsions (HIPEs) have shown potential for probiotic encapsulation, most reported systems mainly provide structural protection and lack multifunctional regulation of gastrointestinal stresses. This study aimed to develop a multifunctional egg-derived HIPEs platform co-stabilized by egg yolk granules (EYGs) and salted egg whites (SEWs), integrating probiotic encapsulation, localized acid-buffering capacity provided by eggshell powder (ESP), and nutritional support to ...

title: Hyaluronic acid in functional foods and oral supplements: linking molecular weight, bioavailability, and food matrix effects to clinical translation.
abstract: Hyaluronic acid (HA) has attracted growing interest as a multifunctional ingredient in functional foods and oral supplements because of its techno-functional properties and proposed benefits for skin and joint health. However, the physiological relevance of orally administered HA remains difficult to interpret because its gastrointestinal fate, exposure, and clinical outcomes may depend on molecular weight distribution, dose, formulation, processing history, food-matrix interactions, and host-re...

title: Functionalized gellan gum hydrogel encapsulating emulsion of probiotic/sea buckthorn oil and co-loading protocatechuic acid for chicken meat preservation.
abstract: Food packaging can effectively reduce food deterioration caused by microbial contamination and adverse storage conditions. In this study, Lactobacillus paracasei Jlus 660321 (LP) was incorporated into a sea buckthorn oil (SBO)-based emulsion and subsequently combined with protocatechuic acid (PCA) in a low-acetyl gellan gum (GG) matrix to construct a multifunctional hydrogel (GPX). GPX showed enhanced mechanical properties and high ABTS and DPPH radical-scavenging activities (>80%). Cell-free su...

title: Probiotic bacterial ghosts enhance oral astaxanthin delivery to alleviate non-alcoholic fatty liver.
abstract: Astaxanthin (AXT) is a promising natural bioactive compound for the nutritional intervention of non-alcoholic fatty liver (NAFL), however, its poor stability and limited oral bioavailability restrict its practical application. In this study, a novel probiotic-derived oral delivery system, designated AXT@LPGs, was developed by loading AXT into Lactiplantibacillus plantarum bacterial ghosts (LPGs) to enhance its efficacy against NAFL. In vivo experiments demonstrated that LPGs significantly improv...

title: High CLA-producing Lactiplantibacillus plantarum MNN1 alleviates irritable bowel syndrome through activation of intestinal PPARα signaling pathway.
abstract: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a common gut-brain axis disorder characterized by visceral hypersensitivity, abdominal pain, and anxiety. Although probiotics have emerged as a promising strategy for IBS management, the specific metabolite-driven mechanisms and their role in gut-brain axis modulation remain largely unclear. In this study, 18 Lactiplantibacillus plantarum strains were screened for conjugated linoleic acid (CLA) production, and strain MNN1 was identified as a high-CLA producer, w...

title: In ovo dose-response characterization of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum HY7715 reveals coordinated physiological and microbiome responses in vivo (Gallus gallus).
abstract: In ovo probiotic delivery provides a controlled in vivo platform for studying early host-microbiome interactions, yet dose-dependent multi-system responses remain insufficiently characterized. This study evaluated a commercially developed strain, Lactiplantibacillus plantarum HY7715 (Lpb. plantarum HY7715 in text, LPHY in figures and sequence ID codes), administered in ovo across a graded dose range (3.2 × 105 to 4.1 × 107 CFU/mL) in Gallus gallus, to assess intestinal development, skeletal musc...

title: AcmA-mediated non-GMO probiotic engineering for functional jujube juice fermentation.
abstract: Probiotics are indispensable functional microorganisms in food fermentation with increasingly promising application prospects. Although genetically modified probiotics show great potential in improving the quality of fermented foods, their practical application is hampered by ethical controversies and safety concerns. To address these issues, the sacB gene encoding levansucrase was cloned from Bacillus atrophaeus in this study. Three non-genetically modified (non-GMO) engineered strains were con...

title: Starch-derived oligosaccharides as prebiotics in innovative functional foods.
abstract: Driven by the escalating demand for innovative functional foods, starch-derived oligosaccharides (SDOs), particularly low-degree-of-polymerization fractions, have emerged as prominent functional carbohydrates, with selected SDO fractions exhibiting prebiotic properties. Their digestive behavior and gut microbial utilization depend strongly on degree of polymerization, glycosidic linkage, and molecular structure. Findings from in vitro and cell-based studies, animal models, and selected human int...

title: Effects of maternal Jussara (Euterpe edulis Mart.) supplementation on metabolic parameters and hypothalamic cytokine markers in male offspring at weaning following maternal trans fat intake.
abstract: Maternal consumption of trans fatty acids (TFA) during pregnancy and lactation is associated with adverse metabolic and hypothalamic cytokine-related alterations in offspring. Anthocyanin-rich fruits such as Jussara (Euterpe edulis Mart.) may counteract these effects through their antioxidant and anti-inflammatory potential. Pregnant Wistar rats (n = 24) were assigned to four diets during pregnancy and lactation: control (C), control +0.5% Jussara (CJ), trans fat-enriched (T), or trans fat + Jus...

title: Encapsulation strategies to enhance the stability and bioaccessibility of bioactive components from tomato by-product extracts for nutraceutical applications.
abstract: Tomato processing generates large volumes of by-products that remain underexploited despite their high content of bioactive compounds with potential health benefits. In this study, the extraction of tomato by-products to produce an extract with neuroprotective-related bioactivity is targeted. Moreover, three encapsulation approaches aimed at increasing the stability of their bioactive compounds were evaluated and compared, namely, spray-drying (SDE), non-modified lecithin liposomes (NLE), and in...

title: Bioprospecting hidden yeasts in artisanal dairies: Revealing potential probiotics for functional fresh cheese.
abstract: Artisanal dairies represent a significant reservoir of microbial biodiversity, offering unique opportunities to discover novel strains with functional properties. This study aimed to isolate and characterize wild yeast strains from traditional sheep cheese production in Central Italy evaluating their probiotic potential and technological suitability for fresh cheese manufacturing. Twenty-five wild yeast strains, belonging to Candida friedrichii, Candida zeylanoydes, Debaryomyces hansenii, Metsch...

title: Encapsulation materials and oral delivery of probiotics: mechanisms, evaluation metrics, and translational perspectives.
abstract: Oral delivery technology is central to enabling the therapeutic and health-modulating functions of probiotics within the intestine, which directly determine the efficacy of probiotics against conditions. However, probiotics face multiple physiological barriers during the oral delivery process which reduce their viability, impair targeting, and severely limit clinical translation. Consequently, the development of efficient and stable encapsulation systems has become a crucial step in advancing pr...

title: Dietary supplement use throughout the colorectal cancer disease trajectory: a prospective cohort study.
abstract: Dietary supplement use is common in the general population, but literature addressing supplement use throughout the disease trajectory in colorectal cancer (CRC) survivors is limited.
journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer

title: Probiotics in type 1 diabetes: immunomodulatory mechanisms and the unresolved question of clinical efficacy.
abstract: Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) is a common autoimmune disease worldwide, which is associated with imbalanced gut microbiota. Intestinal dysbiosis plays a key role in the pathogenesis of T1D, and it may affect immune tolerance and autoimmune responses of pancreatic islet β-cells. As a potential immunomodulator, probiotics can help restore this balance, regulate immune responses, and reduce the risk of T1D. Although probiotics offer a logical immunomodulatory strategy to restore microbial and immune homeos...

title: Biotics-based modulation of gastric precancerous states: microbial, metabolic, and epithelial mechanisms.
abstract: Gastric precancerous states are important intermediate stages in gastric carcinogenesis, yet strategies that directly modify their persistent biological drivers remain limited. Current management mainly includes Helicobacter pylori eradication, endoscopic surveillance, and mucosal protective strategies. Biotics, including probiotics, synbiotics, postbiotics, and next-generation microbial products, have been investigated as potential strategies to modulate persistent microbial, metabolic, inflamm...

title: Oral inulin prebiotic encapsulating Cortex Fraxini extracellular vesicles alleviates colitis and associated renal stress via reinforcing intestinal barriers and remodeling microbiota.
abstract: Background: Gut-kidney axis dysfunction contributes to extraintestinal complications in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), yet effective therapeutic strategies targeting this axis remain limited. This study developed an oral prebiotic delivery system by encapsulating Cortex Fraxini-derived extracellular vesicles (CF-EVs) within an inulin-based hydrogel (CF-EVs@Inulin) and evaluated its therapeutic potential in ulcerative colitis and associated renal injury. Methods: CF-EVs were isolated and chara...

title: Efficacy of a standardized cranberry supplement on overactive bladder symptoms and urobiome alterations in young women: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot trial.
abstract: Urobiome dysbiosis has been implicated in the pathogenesis of overactive bladder (OAB). In this study, the efficacy of a cranberry supplement for OAB symptoms was investigated, and concurrent urobiome alterations were evaluated in young women.
journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology

title: Consumption and knowledge of protein supplements in the Spanish adult population: A cross-sectional survey-based study.
abstract: The popularity of protein supplements (PS) has increased significantly in recent years. Their use is often undertaken without the supervision of a healthcare professional, which may lead to excessive or inappropriate intake and, consequently, pose a health risk.

title: Isolation, Characterization and Molecular Identification of Putative Probiotic Bacteria From Red Tilapia Gut.
abstract: The use of probiotics is a promising strategy to enhance fish health and sustainability in aquaculture as alternatives to antibiotics. This study applied a systematic multi-criteria screening approach to identify autochthonous probiotic candidates from the intestinal microbiota of healthy red tilapia (Oreochromis sp.). A total of 26 culturable bacterial isolates were recovered and evaluated for antimicrobial activity against major fish pathogens (Aeromonas hydrophila, Streptococcus agalactiae an...

title: Genomic and functional characterization of Bacillus siamensis AFSC23 isolated from the gut of European conger (Conger conger) as a probiotic candidate for aquaculture.
abstract: The intestinal microbiota of fish represents a valuable source of antimicrobial and health-promoting bacteria. In this context, we report for the first time the isolation of Bacillus siamensis strain AFSC23 from the intestine of Conger conger. The strain was comprehensively characterized using an integrated genomic and functional approach to assess its safety and probiotic potential in aquaculture. title: The Effect of Acute Beetroot Juice and Caffeine Supplementation on Specific Judo Performance During a Simulated Competition Day in Judo Athletes.
abstract: Beetroot juice (BJ) and caffeine (CAF) are well-established ergogenic aids for exercise performance. However, little is known about their efficacy and interaction within the specific context of a judo competition day. This study investigated the acute effects of BJ, CAF, and their combination (BJCAF) on judo-specific performance across a simulated competition day. Using a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover design, 35 competitive judo athletes (age 23 ± 5 years; body mass 74 ±...

title: Lactobacillus gasseri LG-G12 Alleviates High-Fat Diet-induced Obesity through Gut Microbiota-Bile Acid Axis.
abstract: The role of probiotics in weight management remains controversial. In this study, we found that Lactobacillus gasseri LG-G12 exhibits gut colonization capacity and metabolic regulation potential in vitro. In vivo, LG-G12 alleviated high-fat diet-induced weight gain and visceral fat accumulation in mice. Fecal targeted metabolomics identified bile acid metabolism as a key pathway. Furthermore, LG-G12 might exhibit bile salt hydrolase and hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase activities, contributing to a ...
journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry

title: Assessing the effects of supplementation of vitamins on schizophrenia using Mendelian randomization analysis.
abstract: ObjectiveVitamins are essential for human health and the prevention of diseases. They play an important role in maintaining brain function and mental health, especially in patients with schizophrenia. journal: The Journal of international medical research

title: Synthetic Biology Toolbox for Lactiplantibacillus plantarum: Engineering Next-Generation Probiotic Cell Factories.
abstract: Lactiplantibacillus plantarum has emerged as a promising synthetic biology chassis owing to its food-grade safety, probiotic properties, and adaptability to the gastrointestinal tract. Its engineering potential has expanded rapidly in live biotherapeutics, functional foods, biosensors, and animal health. However, its broader application is still limited by the lack of standardized genetic parts, versatile engineering tools, and industrially compatible chassis. This review summarizes recent advan...

title: Live and Heat-Killed Lactiplantibacillus plantarum HY7715 Attenuate D-Galactose-Induced Aging-Related Brain Changes and Blood-Brain Barrier Disruption with Gut Microbiota Modulation in Mice.
abstract: Aging is associated with changes in systemic homeostasis, intestinal barrier integrity, and brain function. This study investigated the effects of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum HY7715 on aging-related alterations in a D-galactose-induced accelerated aging mouse model. Male C57BL/6J mice were administered D-galactose for 8 weeks and orally treated with live or heat-killed HY7715. D-galactose increased circulating advanced glycation end products (AGEs), blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability, hipp...

title: Gut-targeted interventions to complement PTH-lowering therapy.
abstract: Secondary hyperparathyroidism is a major contributor to skeletal fragility in chronic kidney disease, yet fracture risk remains high despite parathyroid hormone-lowering therapy. In a rat model of chronic kidney disease, Allen et al. showed that combining the prebiotic fiber inulin with a calcimimetic further suppresses elevated bone turnover while improving cortical bone architecture and mechanical properties. These findings highlight the potential of gut-targeted interventions to complement es...

title: Selective recovery effects of short-term beetroot juice supplementation after exercise-induced muscle damage in trained female volleyball players.
abstract: Beetroot juice (BRJ) has been proposed as a nutritional aid for recovery from exercise-induced muscle damage (EIMD), but evidence in female team-sport athletes is limited. It also remains unclear whether any benefit extends across functional, pain-related, swelling, and strength outcomes.
journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

title: Parabacteroides distasonis ameliorates methylphenidate hydrochloride-induced colonic inflammatory responses and associated gastrointestinal distress.
abstract: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a common neurodevelopmental disorder in childhood, with methylphenidate hydrochloride (MPH) as its first-line pharmacotherapy. Though effective, MPH is associated with underrecognized gastrointestinal adverse events warranting further investigation. Recently, the gut microbiota has attracted attention for treating gastrointestinal distress, but research on its role in alleviating MPH-induced gastrointestinal reactions remains scarce.

title: Large-Scale Comparative Genomics of 1,374 Lactiplantibacillus plantarum Genomes Reveals an Open Pan-genome and Strain-Level Variation in Probiotic-Associated and Safety-Related Genomic Features.
abstract: Lactiplantibacillus plantarum is widely studied for food fermentation and probiotic applications, but its functional and safety-related characteristics are strongly strain dependent. Large-scale comparative genomics can characterize this diversity and support genome-informed strain prioritization, although genomic evidence alone does not establish probiotic efficacy or safety. A RefSeq genome collection of L. plantarum was subjected to accession-level auditing, exact-sequence dereplication, and ...

title: Vitamin D Supplementation and Improvement in Insomnia Symptoms Among Malaysian Women With Vitamin D Deficiency: Protocol for a Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract: Insomnia is a prevalent sleep disorder associated with adverse physical, psychological, and functional outcomes. Emerging evidence suggests that vitamin D deficiency may contribute to sleep disturbances. Women are more likely to have lower serum vitamin D (25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D]) levels than men, and they also report a higher prevalence of insomnia. Although several studies have proposed that vitamin D supplementation may improve insomnia symptoms, findings remain inconsistent, and eviden...

title: Prebiotics in sport and exercise: current evidence, practical applications, and methodological considerations.
abstract: Prebiotics are selectively utilized by the host microbiota and can confer health and/or performance benefits, in part through increasing the abundance of beneficial gut microorganisms and their metabolites. While several studies have shown promising initial findings, high-quality scientific evidence examining the effects of prebiotics on athlete performance, health and wellbeing remains limited.
journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

title: Identification of Bioactive Compounds Produced by Probiotic Bacillus coagulans Using Gas Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry.
abstract: Metabolites from probiotic bacteria are gaining wider recognition as bioactive compounds having possible applications in the food, pharmaceutical, and healthcare sectors. Of these, Bacillus coagulans is one of the spore-producing probiotics recognized for its robustness and physiological benefits; however, there is a lack of information regarding the chemical diversity of these bacteria. This study aims to identify the bioactive compounds produced by B. coagulans (MTCC 9872) through the process ...

title: Heat-treated Lactiplantibacillus plantarum MYO Improves Muscle Strength and Modulates Gut Microbiota in Older Adults with Reduced Muscle Strength.
abstract: Age-related sarcopenia is a condition characterized by a decline in muscle strength and physical function with aging, and its improvement is important given its close association with falls, fractures, and mortality. Recently, as the link between age-related gut microbiota dysbiosis and sarcopenia has been elucidated, modulation of the gut microbiota has gained attention as a therapeutic strategy for sarcopenia. title: Subcritical Water in Antimicrobial Benzyl Isothiocyanate Nanoemulsions Preparation and Formulation: A Novel Green Approach for Enhanced Bio-Functionality and Dietary Supplements.
abstract: Benzyl isothiocyanate (BITC) is mainly found in vegetable and fruit seeds with unique biological properties such as anti-cancer and antimicrobial properties. But BITC in pharmaceutical and food formulations faces various challenges, such as low water solubility, environmental instability, and heat sensitivity. This study developed a method based on subcritical water (SW) to prepare BITC nanoemulsion (NE) with desirable activities. Using xanthan and Arabic gums as stabilizers and Tween 80 (T 80) ...

title: Subclinical thiamine deficiency in third-trimester pregnancy despite routine antenatal supplementation: a cross-sectional study in an urban setting, Bangkok, Thailand.
abstract: Thiamine deficiency disorders (TDD) remain a preventable yet underrecognized contributor to maternal and infant morbidity, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. During pregnancy, thiamine deficiency may go undetected despite routine antenatal care and can lead to serious neurological and cardiac complications in breastfed infants. However, data on thiamine status in urban populations receiving standard antenatal supplementation are limited. This study aimed to determine the prevalenc...

title: Effects of feeding a Bacillus-based probiotic to grazing Nellore bulls finished on tropical pasture.
abstract: Interest in probiotics as an alternative to ionophores has increased, particularly in pasture-based systems using energy supplementation. While these additives aim to improve feed efficiency and mitigate acidosis risk, probiotics may also modulate rumen function by enhancing fiber digestion.
